 Honourable Mr. Justice Robin Phukan

Date : 20.01.2023

Heard Mr. A.M. Bora, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. D.K. Baidya,
learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. B.B. Gogoi, learned Addl. P.P. for the State respondent.
This application under section 482 of the Cr.P.C. is preferred by the petitioner, Utpal Bora, for quashing the FIR in connection with CID PS Case No. 01/2023, under sections 13[2]/13[1][b] of Prevention of Corruption Act read with sections 120B/109 of the IPC.

Page No.# 2/6 Be it mentioned here that CID PS Case No. 01/2023, under sections 13[2]/13[1][b] of the PC Act read with sections 120B/109 of the IPC, was registered on the basis of one FIR lodged by Jiaur Rahman, DSP, CID Assam.

The allegation made in the FIR is that in course of investigation of CID PS Case No. 202022, under sections 120B/420/218 IPC read with section 7(b)/8(i)(ii)/12 of the PC Act, it has been found that Utpal Bora has purchased several assets in the last few years and during the period of 01.04.2020 - 31.10.2022, and the value of the assets is found to be beyond of his known source of income, to the tune of 126 Lakhs, which is 948% more than his known source of income, and it has also been found that there was lakhs of transaction which is deposited in his bank account.

sentences.text: Perused the petition and the grounds mentioned there in and also perused the documents placed on record.

Mr. Bora, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that registration of CID PS Case No. 01/2023 is in contravention in Office Memorandum No. PLA[V].139/2009/5, dated 13.11.2009,and no preliminary inquiry was conducted before registration of the FIR and no notice was given to him to submit his response within 30 days and no approval was obtained from the Government, and therefore, Mr. Bora contended to allow this petition.

Mr. Borah further submits that in the event of calling for the case diary, interim protection may be given to the petitioner in the form of 'no coercive action' to be taken against him till receipt of the case diary.
Mr. Borah further submits that the petitioner and his wife has been served notice under section 41(A) Cr.P.C. today morning and as such he has apprehension of arrest.

Mr. Borah further submits that on earlier occasion, this court, in Crl.Pet.No.801/2017, dated 20.09.2017, has granted relief due to non compliance of the mandate of the Page No.# 3/6 said Office Memorandum.

On the other hand, Mr. Gogoi, learned Addl. P.P. has vehemently opposed the petition, and also in granting interim protection to the petitioner, on the ground that the aforesaid Office Memorandum relates to cases under the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption only and the same will not be applicable to the CID cases and that the offences against the petitioners are serious in nature.

Having heard learned counsel for both the parties, I have carefully gone through the petition and the documents placed on record and also perused the office memorandum which is annexed with the petition as Annexure No. II and the notice under section 41A issued to the petitioner and his wife and also the FIR dated 09.01.2023.
Let the notice be issued to the respondents returnable in 2 weeks.

Since Mr. Gogoi, learned Addl.
P.P. has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the State respondent, no formal notice is required to be issued.
However, extra requisite copy of the petition be furnished to her during the course of the day.
Mr. Gogoi shall produce the case diary before this court on the next date, and file his reply if so advised.

The law regarding granting of interim relief in the form of 'no coercive action' to be taken against the petitioner, is well settled by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M/S Neeharika, Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. the State of Maharashtra& Ors.

Mahesh Cooperative Urban Bank Shareholders Welfare Association vs. Ramesh Kumar Bung and others reported in [2021] 9 SCC 152, where it has been held that granting of interim protection to the petitioner, in a petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. or under article 226 of the Page No.# 4/6 Constitution of India.

sentences.text: In M/S Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (Supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the parameters laid down from Point No.I - XV in paragraph No. 23, would be applicable.
It is further held that, an interim order of stay of investigation during the pendency of the quashing petition can be passed with the circumspection.

sentences.text: Such an interim order should not required to be passed routinely, casually and/or mechanically.

Normally, when the investigation is in progress and the facts are hazy and the entire evidence/material is not before the High Court, the High Court should restrain itself from passing the interim order of not to arrest or "no coercive steps to be adopted" and the accused should be relegated to apply for anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Cr.P.C. before the competent court.

The High Court shall not and as such is not justified in passing the order of not to arrest and/or "no coercive steps" either during the investigation or till the investigation is completed and/or till the final report/chargesheet is filed under section 173 Cr.P.C. while dismissing/disposing of the quashing petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Further, in the said case, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that even in a case where the High Court is prima facie of the opinion that an exceptional case is made out for grant of interim stay of further investigation, after considering the broad parameters while exercising the powers under section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under article 226 of the Constitution of India referred to hereinabove the High Court has to give brief reasons why such an interim order is warranted and/or is required to be passed so that it can demonstrate the application of mind by the Court and the higher forum can consider what was weighed with the High Court while passing such an interim order.
Page No.# 5/6

In the instant case, in the Office Memorandum, dated 30.11.2009, it is stated that notwithstanding anything contained in any provision of earlier Office Memorandum in this regard,
the Enquiry Officer through the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption shall collect the details of income and expenditure as well as other requirements such as assets and liabilities from the suspect officer/employee.

If the suspect officer/employee fails to respond to furnishing the required information/statements etc. within 30 days from the date of receipt of requisition from the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption, the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption shall move to the Government in the Political Department for approval to register a criminal case against the defaulting suspect officer/employee.

sentences.text: Indisputably, in the case in hand, while registering the aforesaid case against the petitioner, no notice was given to him and no approval was obtained to register a complaint or register a criminal case against the petitioner.

But, as submitted by Mr. Gogoi, learned Addl. P.P. the Office Memorandum No. PLA[V].139/2009/5, dated 13.11.2009, seems to be applicable only in the case of Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption and admittedly, there is no indication in the said Office Memorandum regarding applicability of the same, in cases of CID and other Police Station also.

entities.text: Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Being so, this court is unable to record concurrence with the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner.

And having carefully considered the submission of learned counsel for both the parties and also considering the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases discussed herein above, in respect of interim relief, this court is of the prima facie opinion that no exceptional case is made out for granting interim relief as prayed for, in the form of 'no coercive steps' to be adopted.
Accordingly, the prayer of interim relief is declined.

Though this court Page No.# 6/6 was pleased to grant interim relief in Crl.Pet.No.801/2017, dated 20.09.2017, due to non compliance of the Office Memorandum, yet, the said case was covered by the Office Memorandum, as it was a case of Utpal Bora vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136077174/

and vigilance.
Therefore, to the considered opinion of this court, the same would not come into aid of the petitioner.

It well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in the case of Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) & Anr. Vs. Thommundru Hannah Vijoylakshmi, Crl. Appeal No. 1045 of 2021, that preliminary enquiry in corruption cases is not mandatory.

entities.text: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) & Anr. Vs. Thommundru Hannah Vijoylakshmi, Crl. Appeal No. 1045 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in State Of West Bengal & Ors vs. Swapan Kumar Guha & Ors., reported in (1982) 1 SCC 561, that "right of inquiry is conditioned by the existence of reason to suspect the commission of a cognizable offence and they cannot, reasonably, have reason so to suspect unless the F.I.R., prima facie,
discloses the commission of such offence.

entities.text: State Of West Bengal & Ors vs. Swapan Kumar Guha & Ors., reported in (1982) 1 SCC 561
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If that condition is satisfied, the investigation must go on.

The Court has then no power to stop the investigation, for to do so would be to trench upon the lawful power to investigate into cognizable offences".
